concreteBlockingFindings.finding: Marker delivery can satisfy the logging checks while actual non-marker production is zero; encoded delivery is checked only as a sum across all consoles.
sourceFacts: PRODUCT_EVENTS increments for every non-marker callback without distinguishing application logger identity or duplicate additive deliveries.
countOnlyReport prints the product-event delta; finishCase never requires this delta to be positive.

probeRoutes requires a positive aggregate console byte-size delta, so one producing console can hide another console with no delivered marker. No per-console produced encoded-event count is enforced or reported.

The supplementary raw appender is attached to every logger. Raw callback totals can count the same event at multiple additive attachments; these are delivery counts, not unique application event counts.
concreteBlockingFindings.consequence: The source permits quiet actual logging targets to receive zero-hit credit from nonsensitive marker production alone, contrary to the required actual RAW and ORIGINAL-encoded produced-positive counts.
concreteBlockingFindings.requiredCorrection: Keep nonsensitive ROOT/application markers as support. Bind required actual non-marker raw production and original encoded production to each applicable case and original console route; fail unavailable/zero production rather than accepting quiet targets. Preserve attachment multiplicity separately from unique event counts. Validate each required console delivery instead of only a summed byte delta. Do not add a fake encoder or new product/service calls.

concreteBlockingFindings.finding: The release prerequisite does not inspect newly produced status errors or prove newly registered routes deliver before returning the actual provider value; status inventory can silently miss same-size turnover.
sourceFacts: Status inspection occurs during initial installation and case/class finish, but not at beginCase after setup/probes or in FaultCase.release.
FaultCase.release calls verifyRoutes(false) and tests the existing FAILURES count. verifyRoutes does not inspect StatusManager errors or probe delivery.
verifyRoutes(false) can register a newly existing inherited logger during release without probing that route.
inspectStatus uses only list size and a numeric cursor. A replacement snapshot with the same size leaves no new entry inspected and no drift failure.

Several prerequisite branches throw a closed diagnostic without incrementing FAILURES. beginCase catch exports FAILURES+1 but does not persist that increment. This does not implement a universal sticky prerequisite failure ledger.
concreteBlockingFindings.consequence: A status ERROR created after the initial preflight can be discovered only after actual release. Equal-size status replacement can remain unobserved. The required fail-before-release and sticky drift/status contract is incomplete.
concreteBlockingFindings.requiredCorrection: Immediately before actual provider return, independently check supported route identity, required marker delivery, status errors and capture drops/overflow; persist prerequisite failure counts. Reject route/status turnover that cannot be fully inspected, including equal-size replacement. Keep this source-only observer work free of additional provider/service/SQL/auth operations.

concreteBlockingFindings.finding: The actual relay callback has unowned error-graph and late-close exits outside the closed failure disposition.
sourceFacts: A Throwable caught before Scenario identification is neither retained in the preregistered peerCase nor scanned nor counted as an observation failure.
The fallback sendResponseHeaders IOException is discarded without observation.

exchange.close executes before peer exit accounting and ThreadLocal removal, with no nested guard/finally. An unchecked close failure bypasses those operations and can escape into the executor as the original Throwable.
Method/template invocation interception protects the test thread; it does not intercept this relay executor callback.
concreteBlockingFindings.consequence: An owned relay error can disappear from the actual error-graph inventory, and a late-close failure can escape without a fixed enum/count-only diagnostic. Incomplete peer accounting may retain quarantine but does not itself provide the missing closed export boundary.
concreteBlockingFindings.requiredCorrection: Use the preregistered actual peer ledger for errors before Scenario lookup and for original response/close errors. Observe them transiently without replacing Scenario.failure or original expected product errors. Preserve original forwarding/order/status behavior; put exit accounting and ThreadLocal removal in an independent finally and prevent any unexpected owned callback exit from exporting its original cause/content. Export only a fresh fixed-code numeric AssertionError with null cause and no suppressed originals; retain quarantine if real peer/owner closure is unsafe.

concreteBlockingFindings.finding: The final scan is not guaranteed before disposal after a restoration/status/scanner failure.
sourceFacts: finishClass scans before restoration, then calls restore, sets restored=true, inspects status, and scans again.
If post-restoration inspectStatus or scanAll throws, the catch captures that new Throwable and increments failure counts but does not run another independent scan.
The finally block then wipes SINKS and quarantine and disposes all ledgers whenever restored is true, including that failure path.
If restore itself throws, the newly captured restoration Throwable is not scanned in this method before exit; quarantine is retained, but the required always-finally scan has not occurred.
concreteBlockingFindings.consequence: Newly captured late-close/restoration failure fields can be erased before being compared with actual releases. The closed JUnit outcome fails, but the demanded scan-before-disposal contract is still violated.
concreteBlockingFindings.requiredCorrection: Place independent bounded scans of applicable captured fields and actual late errors in a finally phase before any wipe/reference release. Continue other scans when one observation fails, record unavailability with sticky fixed counts, and keep quarantine/ledger ownership until real closure and required final scans are complete. Do not use successful restoration alone as permission to dispose after a failed terminal scan.
